title: Ghana Empire (Wagadu)
summary: Ghana, called Wagadu in Soninke tradition, may have begun its rise in the fourth century as a city-state in the grasslands between the Senegal and Niger rivers, and flourished from at least the sixth to the thirteenth century. Its kings, probably ruling from Koumbi Saleh in today's Mauritania, grew rich on gold, which they traded with Arab and Berber merchants for salt, horses and cloth. Weakened after an Almoravid defeat in 1076 and a Susu attack in 1203, its remnants passed to Mali by 1240.

uncertainty.note: Oral traditions and chronicles estimate the empire began in the 4th century (c. 300 CE) or by the 6th century; it was eclipsed following Almoravid pressure and absorbed into the Mali Empire by c. 1240.

where.modern_name: Koumbi Saleh, Hodh Ech Chargi, Mauritania (probable capital site; the empire spanned southeastern Mauritania, western Mali, and eastern Senegal)
where.historical_name: Koumbi Saleh, capital of the Ghana Empire (Wagadu)

importance.justification: The first great West African trading empire, linking the gold of the south to trans-Saharan trade (R3 D3 T3 L3).
